observations: Maintained native WebAuthn verification with actual UV enforcement, server-owned registration context, physical user/key/session generation pins and independently committed one-use challenge consumption.

Real built-app browser uses actual Chromium CTAP2 virtual authenticators, native cookies and isolated PostgreSQL without HTTP route or verifier mocks. Genuine non-UV registration/authentication responses and their replays are refused.

Actual replacement-session insertion failure after successful verified key writing rolls back key, generation and session changes; the genuine prior session survives and the consumed nonce remains unusable. A fixture-only PostgreSQL sequence proves that write point was reached.

Actual SDK and HTTP error paths retain static metadata without forwarding raw authentication errors. The lower-router negative control inspects Error messages using Node inspect; JSON.stringify(Error) alone does not qualify a negative control.
Final UI compilation includes tests. Production UI build is exercised by the browser. Evidence logs exclude earlier staged browser logs containing disposable WebAuthn wire metadata.
limits: Local-account canonical RP software/emulated-authenticator qualification only. Enterprise-bound users are withheld pending full enterprise recovery and verified first-factor policy integration.
Configured-operator domain admission/bootstrap, other powerful actions, full V10 privacy/workflow/portability and remaining product work stay open.
No physical authenticator, external IdP, SaaS email, deployed replicas/restarts, representative Human, host or production qualification.
Latest complete workspace typecheck/test/build and complete V10 acceptance remain required before PR-ready hand-off. No PR, merge or deployment readiness claim.
